\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Noise Kernel}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.NoiseKernel
\section{Overview}
Conditional expectations, orthogonal components, and spectral noise admit explicit finite resampling kernels. For noise rates between zero and one the resulting operator contracts the absolute first moment.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional expectation kernel]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_kernel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with coordinate weights $w_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $E_Sf(x)=\sum_y[\prod_{i\in S}\mathbf1_{x_i=y_i}\prod_{i\notin S}w_i(y_i)]f(y)$ for every $x\in\Omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Alternating expansion of product kernels]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.signed_product_kernel}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For a finite set $I$, $S\subseteq I$, and real functions $a,b$ on $I$, $\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}\prod_{i\in T}a_i\prod_{i\notin T}b_i=\prod_{i\in S}(a_i-b_i)\prod_{i\notin S}b_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Orthogonal component kernel]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component_kernel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.signed_product_kernel}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with coordinate weights $w_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Its orthogonal component satisfies $f_S(x)=\sum_y[\prod_{i\in S}(\mathbf1_{x_i=y_i}-w_i(y_i))\prod_{i\notin S}w_i(y_i)]f(y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral noise kernel]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_kernel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with coordinate weights $w_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $T_\rho f(x)=\sum_y[\prod_i(\rho\mathbf1_{x_i=y_i}+(1-\rho)w_i(y_i))]f(y)$ for every $x\in\Omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute first moment contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_norm_one_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\|T_\rho f\|_{1,P}\le\|f\|_{1,P}$.
\end{theorem}
